annotations.title: What can I do with this property?

description: Use when someone asks what they can do with a specific property or address in the US, or what it is zoned. In Austin, TX and Nashville, TN it answers in full: what the lot is zoned and what that means, how many homes the lot can take (Austin HOME rules, Texas SB 840 apartments on commercial land), what the zoning ordinance or Nashville Specific Plan says, whether a short-term rental (Airbnb) is allowed, the property tax and flood risk, with a map link and a printable brief link. For a Nashville or Austin lot, when the paid Lot File is on sale in that city and covers the lot, it also returns lot_file: what the cited file adds (documents read, rules computed for the lot, pending cases) and the link to buy it. Any other US address or point gets the free nationwide answer (status ok_free): the zoning district, its description, overlays, the parcel id and the zoning ordinance link, read live from the jurisdiction's own public layers where MapLedger's registry has them (tier B), or what the records show, such as a Texas county with no zoning authority (tier C). Every free line names its source. Takes an address with its city and state, or a latitude and longitude.

address.description: Street address, for example '1600 E 6th St' or '1600 Division St, 37203'

appraised_value.description: Appraised value in dollars for the tax estimate (defaults: Austin 550000, Nashville 450000)

city.description: "austin" (City of Austin, Texas) or "nashville" (Nashville and Davidson County, Tennessee) for the full answer. Any other US city or county, for example "Phoenix, AZ", gets the free nationwide answer.

homestead.description: Austin only: the owner's main home, so homestead exemptions apply (default true)

property_class.description: Nashville only: taxed as a home (25%) or a business (40%); default follows the zoning

name: land_at

code.description: ok_free tier B: where the zoning ordinance is published

jurisdiction.description: ok_free only: the city or county that zones the point, from MapLedger's registry or the Census geography

lines.description: ok_free: one definitive sentence per fact, each naming its source

lot.description: The lot's own records: size (Austin) or land use, building year, street frontage, service district and permit counts (Nashville)

lot_file.description: Nashville and Austin, when the file is on sale in that city and covers the lot's zoning: the paid Lot File for this lot, what it adds to this answer, and where to buy it

parcel.description: ok_free tier B: the parcel id and its source layer

reason.description: ok_free tier C: why there is no live zoning answer

retry_after_seconds.description: rate_limited only: seconds until the allowance resets

short_term_rentals.description: Owner-occupied and whole-home short-term rental answers for this spot, each with its reason and source

specific_plan.description: Nashville Specific Plan: what its ordinance says

status.description: ok: answered in full (Austin or Nashville); ok_free: the free nationwide answer for another US place, with tier, jurisdiction and lines; choose: the address matches more than one place, choices lists them; not_found: no such address; no_zoning: the point is a street, water or outside the city; unsupported_city: the Census geocoder found no US address or place for the input; rate_limited: this caller's hourly allowance of nationwide answers is spent

tier.description: ok_free only. B: the jurisdiction's own zoning and parcel layers answered live. C: what the records show, with no live layer answer

what_you_can_build.description: Austin: how many homes the lot can take

zoning.description: The zoning code, what it means, overlays and the ordinance behind it; for ok_free tier B, the district, its description, overlays and source layer

zoning_ordinances.description: Austin zoning ordinances covering the point, newest first
